chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muyassir said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man buys a skin of oil and finds dregs (sediment) in it. He said: 'If he is someone who knows that dregs are usually in the oil, he does not have the right to return it; and if he does not know, he has the right to return it.'

key_terms.دُرْدِيّاً: dregs, sediment, or lees found at the bottom of oil
key_terms.زِقَّ زَيْتٍ: a skin or container of oil
key_terms.يَرُدَّهُ: to return it (exercise the right of return due to defect)

ai.seo_question: When can a buyer return oil containing sediment according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *khiyar al-‘ibah* (option of defect) by distinguishing between known customary defects and hidden ones, a key distinction in Shia fiqh regarding fair trade. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on transparency and the buyer's reasonable expectation, ensuring that sellers cannot exploit ignorance of common impurities like *durdiyya* (sediment) to enforce a sale. This ruling underscores the ethical obligation in Shia jurisprudence to align commercial transactions with the spirit of justice (*‘adl*) and mutual consent.
